title: build.chunkImportMap on an environment is ignored by vite:build-import-analysis under builder.sharedPlugins
body:
### Describe the bug

An SSR app can only enable the import map for the client: the server runtime (workerd, in our case) resolves static specifiers against disk and has no import-map support. That configuration silently produces a broken client bundle, and the obvious alternative crashes the build.

**1. `environments.client.build.chunkImportMap` is ignored.** `vite:build-import-analysis` reads the root config it captured at construction, not the environment being built (`dist/node/chunks/node.js:28283` in 8.1.5):

```js
function buildImportAnalysisPlugin(config) {   // root resolved config
  if (config.build.chunkImportMap) {           // not this.environment.config.build
    importMapMapping = getImportMap(bundle, config).mapping
```

With `builder.sharedPlugins` one plugin container serves every environment build, so that value stays the root one while rolldown gets the environment's. The mapping is then never applied — and it is the only way to resolve those specifiers, since chunk *code* holds placeholders while the *bundle* is keyed by real filenames. `addDeps` finds nothing and every `__VITE_PRELOAD__` marker becomes `[]`:

```js
// broken: no dep list, so __vitePreload injects no stylesheet link
// (real output is minified: `k(async()=>{…},[])`)
await __vitePreload(async () => { await import("./lazy-BoslDmDy.js") }, [])
```

The lazy chunk's CSS is emitted and referenced by nothing, so the component renders unstyled in production. Nothing warns. On our app this is 0 dep lists and 29 of 32 stylesheets unreferenced, versus 1552 and 0 with the option at the root.

`sharedPlugins` is set by the framework, not the app — `@tanstack/start-plugin-core` sets it in `dist/esm/vite/plugin.js`. Without it Vite re-resolves the config per environment build and the two views agree, which is probably why this hasn't come up.

Expected: read the option from the environment being built. The same root read is in `vite:css-post` (both branches) and `vite:build-html`'s `postImportMapHook`.

**2. Moving the option to the root, with the server environment opted out, crashes.** `getImportMap()` is documented to return `undefined` when the map is absent from the bundle, but all three call sites dereference it — `.mapping` twice in `vite:css-post`, `.source` in `postImportMapHook`. A server bundle legitimately has no map asset:

```
[plugin vite:css-post]
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'mapping')
    at PluginContextImpl.generateBundle (vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:22347:76)
```

Both are in the same repro because fixing (1) that way runs into (2). Happy to split them.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/antur84/vite-chunk-import-map-repro

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
npm install && npm run verify
```

`verify.mjs` builds a client + ssr project across the two axes and checks whether the lazy chunk's CSS is reachable at runtime. On 8.2.0 the two failing cells are the two bugs:

```
SCOPE=off         sharedPlugins=0   ok      depLists=1 emptyDepLists=0 lazyCssReachable=true
SCOPE=environment sharedPlugins=0   ok      depLists=1 emptyDepLists=0 lazyCssReachable=true
SCOPE=root        sharedPlugins=0   ok      depLists=1 emptyDepLists=0 lazyCssReachable=true
SCOPE=off         sharedPlugins=1   ok      depLists=1 emptyDepLists=0 lazyCssReachable=true
SCOPE=environment sharedPlugins=1   BROKEN  depLists=0 emptyDepLists=1 lazyCssReachable=false
SCOPE=root        sharedPlugins=1   BUILD FAILED — TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'mapping')
```

On 8.1.5 only the first fails; the crash there needs a pure-CSS chunk in the server bundle, which this minimal project doesn't produce but our real app does.

### System Info

```shell
  System:
    OS: macOS 26.5.2
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.14.1
    npm: 11.11.0
  npmPackages:
    vite: ^8.2.0 => 8.2.0
```

Also reproduced on vite 8.1.5 / rolldown 1.1.5.

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

From a build with `console.error` added inside `vite:build-import-analysis`'s `generateBundle`, client environment, option on `environments.client.build`:

```
[bia-entry]  { env: 'client', consumer: 'client', insertPreload: true,
               rootOpt: false, envOpt: true, sameBuildObject: false }
[bia-branch] { branchTaken: false, mapAssetPresent: true }
[bia-site]   { url: './DomainsTab-BpOcm4c_.js', normalizedFile: 'assets/DomainsTab-BpOcm4c_.js',
               mappingSize: null, mappedTo: null, inBundleDirect: false, depsSize: 0 }
```

Same build with the option at the root: `rootOpt: true`, `branchTaken: true`, `mappingSize: 3514`, `depsSize: 84`. `inBundleDirect: false` in both is the reason the mapping is load-bearing.

### Validations

- [X] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitejs/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [X] Read the [docs](https://vite.dev/guide).
- [X] Check that there isn't already an issue that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. (#22567, #22740 and #22946 are the adjacent closed chunkImportMap CSS issues; this is neither — the map is correct here, it is the preload dep lists that are empty.)

- [X] Check that this is a concrete bug.

---

Investigated with AI assistance. The mechanism was confirmed by patching vite's dist to log `config.build.chunkImportMap` against the environment's during real builds, and the repro was reduced by bisecting config axes one at a time; every number and log line above is from an actual run, on both 8.1.5 and 8.2.0.

title: `build.lib` without `entry`: a second build with a different `input` still builds the first entry
body:
### Describe the bug

When `build.lib` is set without an `entry`, resolving the config writes the top-level `input` into the user's own `lib` object. If the same config object is used again for another build with a different `input`, the new input is silently ignored and the first entry is built again.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-uscwzq3e?file=repro.mjs

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir lib-repro && cd lib-repro
pnpm init
pnpm add -D vite
mkdir src
echo "export const who = 'I am A'" > src/a.js
echo "export const who = 'I am B'" > src/b.js
```

`repro.mjs`:

```js
import { build } from 'vite'

const shared = {
  logLevel: 'error',
  configFile: false,

    lib: { formats: ['es'] }, // no entry, falls back to the top-level `input`

}

await build({ ...shared, input: 'src/a.js' })

const result = await build({ ...shared, input: 'src/b.js' })
```

```
user lib object after first build: { formats: [ 'es' ], entry: 'src/a.js' }
second build output:
//#region src/a.js
```

title: Dynamic Imports don't resolve when using package.json#imports
body:
### Describe the bug

In SvelteKit 3.0 we are deprecating the alias `$lib` (which uses `resolve.alias` under the hood) in favour of a platform feature: `package.json#imports`.

You can define this in your package.json

```json
{
	"imports": {
		"#lib/*": "./src/lib/*"
	}
}
```
and it basically acts as an alias (you can do `import("#lib/my-file.js")` at whatever nesting level and it will resolve correctly).

The base import works fine but where it fails is when you are using dynamic imports with vite:

```ts
// this will fail
await import(`#lib/${folder_name}/index.ts`);

// the same with alias works fine
await import(`$lib/${folder_name}/index.ts`);

// same if I import using a relative path
await import(`../../lib/${folder_name}/index.ts`);
```

given the rest works fine this feels like a bug worth addressing.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-pj6f16ta?file=vite.config.ts,src%2Fmain.js,package.json,src%2Flib%2Falias%2Fa%2Findex.ts,src%2Flib%2Falias%2Fb%2Findex.ts,src%2Flib%2Fimportmaps%2Fa%2Findex.ts,src%2Flib%2Fimportmaps%2Fb%2Findex.ts&terminal=dev

### Steps to reproduce

1. open the playground
2. run the app
3. check that you get a warning in terminal the console
4. try to press the "load alias" button and verify it works
5. try to press the "load import without importmaps" and verify it works
6. try to press the "load import" and verify it doesn't work

### System Info


title: Regression in 8.2: Vitest `setupFiles` fails with "Cannot find module" across Windows drive symlinks
body:
### Describe the bug

I am running a Vitest test suite on Windows where my project directory is accessed via a symlink across different drive letters (e.g., executing in `C:\D-Data\...` which is symlinked to `D:\.Data\...`).

When updating Vite from `8.1.5` to `8.2.0/1`, running Vitest fails immediately with `Error: Cannot find module '/vitest.setup.js'`.  
I believe that the path resolution for `setupFiles` gets stripped down to the absolute root of the C: drive when resolving across the symlinked drives.

Rolling Vite back to `8.1.5` completely resolves the issue without any configuration changes.

I strongly suspect this regression was introduced in `v8.2.0-beta.0` by PR #22832 (`resolve root to real path`), which may be incorrectly forcing the root to the real path (D:) and failing to respect the execution context or `preserveSymlinks: true` when Vitest attempts to load the virtual module.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/ELowry/Vite-Symlink-Issue-Test-Repo

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone this repository on a Windows machine to a secondary drive (e.g., `D:\.Data\vite-symlink-windows-bug`).
2. Open an Administrator command prompt and create a directory junction/symlink on the primary drive pointing to it: 
   `mklink /J C:\D-Data\vite-symlink-windows-bug D:\.Data\vite-symlink-windows-bug`

title: SSR transform: imported binding used as a computed key in a defaulted destructured parameter is not rewritten (ReferenceError)
`bundleConfigFile` incorrectly resolves source map path under certain conditions
body: ### Describe the bug The [`path.resolve` call inside of the `sourcemapPathTransform` callback in `bundleConfigFile`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b4d66fee14d970f45b8a6f3d7d6aee73ca9b88ab/packages/vite/src/node/config.ts#L2656) fails to resolve the correct configuration file path under certain circumstances (e.g., VitePress) due to incorrectly treating the last path segment as a directory, rather than a file. This sometimes results in the source map containing an incorrect path to the source file, which breaks debugging functionality in the config, as well as any plugins the config imports. # VitePress Behavior Below is a screenshot of `bundleConfigFile` when resolving a VitePress config file: Note the double `.vitepress` in the path, which is incorrect (It should just be `/home/wakeful-cloud/Downloads/test/.vitepress/config.mts`). When I decode the base64-encoded source map at the bottom of the compiled config file, I predictably get a sourcemap with an incorrect path: ```json { "version": 3, "file": "config.js", "names": [], "sources": [ "/home/wakeful-cloud/Downloads/test/.vitepress/.vitepress/config.mts" ], "sourcesContent": [ "import { defineConfig } from 'vitepress'\n\n// https://vitepress.dev/reference/site-config\nexport default defineConfig({\n title: \"My Awesome Project\",\n description: \"A VitePress Site\",\n vite: {\n plugins: [\n {\n name: \"test\",\n configResolved: config => {\n console.log(\"Vite config resolved:\", config);\n }\n }\n ]\n },\n themeConfig: {\n // https://vitepress.dev/reference/default-theme-config\n nav: [\n { text: 'Home', link: '/' },\n { text: 'Examples', link: '/markdown-examples' }\n ],\n\n sidebar: [\n {\n text: 'Examples',\n items: [\n { text: 'Markdown Examples', link: '/markdown-examples' },\n { text: 'Runtime API Examples', link: '/api-examples' }\n ]\n }\n ],\n\n socialLinks: [\n { icon: 'github', link: 'https://github.com/vuejs/vitepress' }\n ]\n }\n})\n" ], "mappings": ";;AAGA,IAAA,iBAAe,aAAa;CAC1B,OAAO;CACP,aAAa;CACb,MAAM,EACJ,SAAS,CACP;EACE,MAAM;EACN,iBAAgB,WAAU;GACxB,QAAQ,IAAI,yBAAyB,MAAM;EAC7C;CACF,CACF,EACF;CACA,aAAa;EAEX,KAAK,CACH;GAAE,MAAM;GAAQ,MAAM;EAAI,GAC1B;GAAE,MAAM;GAAY,MAAM;EAAqB,CACjD;EAEA,SAAS,CACP;GACE,MAAM;GACN,OAAO,CACL;IAAE,MAAM;IAAqB,MAAM;GAAqB,GACxD;IAAE,MAAM;IAAwB,MAAM;GAAgB,CACxD;EACF,CACF;EAEA,aAAa,CACX;GAAE,MAAM;GAAU,MAAM;EAAqC,CAC/D;CACF;AACF,CAAC" } ``` # Vanilla Vite Behavior Interestingly, vanilla (i.e., non-VitePress) Vite does not experience this bug by coincidence. title: CSS minify: build.target "esnext" passes targets: {} to Lightning CSS, which reads it as "nothing is supported"
body:
# CSS minify: `build.target: "esnext"` passes `targets: {}` to Lightning CSS, which reads it as "nothing is supported"

**Vite:** 8.2.0
**Affects:** `build.cssMinify` default path (Lightning CSS)

## Description

With `build.target: "esnext"` (and therefore `build.cssTarget: "esnext"`), Vite calls Lightning
CSS with `targets: {}` rather than `targets: undefined`.

Lightning CSS treats an empty targets object differently from an absent one: `{}` means "no
browser supports anything", so compatibility lowering runs. `undefined` means "no constraints"
and leaves modern syntax alone. Users who set `esnext` are explicitly asking for the latter.

`convertTargets` skips `esnext` entries and returns the accumulated object, which for a
target list of exactly `["esnext"]` is `{}`:

```js
for (const entry of entriesWithoutES) {
  if (entry === "esnext") continue;
  // ...
}
return targets; // {} when every entry was "esnext"
```

`minifyCSS` then passes that straight through:

```js
targets: convertTargets(config.build.cssTarget),
```

## Impact

Two problems:

1. `esnext` users get compatibility transforms they opted out of.
2. It exposes them to a Lightning CSS bug where rules are silently dropped —
   see https://github.com/parcel-bundler/lightningcss/issues/1310.

In our case this silently deleted three CSS rules from a production build. The pattern was:

```css
.card:hover { --icon-bg: blue }
.card:hover,
.card:open:not([data-closing]) { --bg: gray }
```

The `:open` half disappeared from the minified output with no warning. Dev was fine, so it
went unnoticed. Switching to `build.cssMinify: "esbuild"` restored it.

## Suggested fix

Pass `undefined` when the converted targets object has no keys:

```js
const converted = convertTargets(config.build.cssTarget)
targets: Object.keys(converted).length ? converted : undefined,
```

That makes `esnext` mean "no constraints" for CSS, matching what it means for JS.

## Note

`build.cssMinify: "esbuild"` is a working workaround, but esbuild is only an *optional* peer
dependency of Vite 8. Projects relying on it need to declare it themselves, or the escape
hatch breaks whenever a transitive dependency stops providing it.

## Related

`convertTargets` was previously fixed for unknown ES-year targets in #17983. That fix
extended the ES-to-browser map; it does not cover `esnext`, which still yields `{}`.

title: `build.license` attributes the wrong version and omits license text for packages with nested `package.json` type markers
body:
### Describe the bug

`build.license` resolves each bundled module to its package via
`findNearestMainPackageData`. For packages that ship a dual ESM/CJS build with a bare
type-marker `package.json` in a subdirectory, resolution stops at the marker instead of
the real package root. The emitted license file then reports `0.0.0` as the version and
carries no license text or SPDX identifier for those packages.

This matters more than a normal metadata glitch: the output of this option is an
attribution notice. A file that names a dependency with a fabricated version and no
license text does not discharge the notice clause it exists to satisfy, and it fails
silently — there is nothing in the output to indicate the entry is incomplete.

### Reproduction

Any package with this layout reproduces it. `socket.io-client` and its transitive deps
are a convenient case:

```
node_modules/engine.io-client/package.json              → name, version 6.6.3, license MIT, LICENSE file
node_modules/engine.io-client/build/esm/package.json    → {"name":"engine.io-client","type":"module","browser":{…}}
```

With `build.license` enabled and `socket.io-client` imported, the emitted file contains:

```
## @socket.io/component-emitter - 0.0.0     (actual: 3.1.2, MIT)
## engine.io-client - 0.0.0                 (actual: 6.6.3, MIT)
## engine.io-parser - 0.0.0                 (actual: 5.2.3, MIT)
## socket.io-client - 4.8.3                 (version correct; no identifier, no text)
```

`socket.io-client` differs because its own marker happens to include `version`.

### Root cause

`findNearestMainPackageData` recurses upward only while `name` is absent:

```js
function findNearestMainPackageData(basedir, packageCache) {
  const nearestPackage = findNearestPackageData(basedir, packageCache);
  return nearestPackage && (nearestPackage.data.name
    ? nearestPackage
    : findNearestMainPackageData(path.dirname(nearestPackage.dir), packageCache));
}
```

A type-marker manifest carrying `name` but no `version` satisfies that predicate, so it
is treated as the main package data. The license plugin then reads
`{ name, version = '0.0.0', license }` from the marker and looks for a license file in
the marker's directory, where there isn't one.

### Suggested fix

Requiring `version` as well as `name` before accepting a manifest as the main package
data would resolve it. If tightening the shared helper is undesirable — other callers may
legitimately want a name-only match — the license plugin could keep walking upward while
`version` is missing, or resolve the package root from the last `node_modules/` path
segment instead.

Either way it would be worth having the plugin surface incomplete entries rather than
emitting them, since the failure is otherwise invisible in the output.

Related precedent: #19324 handled the adjacent case of a `package.json` without `name`
reaching `resolveLibCssFilename`. This is the `name`-without-`version` variant, surfacing
in a different consumer.

### Environment

Observed on `vite@7.3.1` and on a Rolldown-based Vite 8 distribution; the plugin
implementation is identical in both. pnpm 10.11.1, Node 22, Linux.
